correctness.rationale: For every t>=2 and every n_i>=3, cut-vertex separation reduces global minimality to independent anchored cycle minimality. The cyclic-gap lemma is proved in both directions, and two nonconsecutive marks yield a disjoint-gap contradiction for anchored minimal sets with >=3 nonhub marks. Exact stars-and-bars and inclusion-exclusion give local b(n) pairs, plus exactly one even antipode. Multiplication yields the claim; all stated boundary cases including C3 and C4 are covered. Actual standalone verifier exhaustively compared complete families of minimal sets on 28 instances/104644 nonempty subsets. Computational scope is finite; the full proof is combinatorial.

value.rationale: The exact all-size classification addresses the natural minimal-geodetic-set enumeration problem studied in primary metric-graph literature; it is not a known-minimum recomputation. It gives explicit counts for arbitrary cycle lengths and number of petals, an exact upper geodetic number and complete size spectrum, an unbounded difference between minimum and upper values and a real-rooted/log-concave polynomial, all derived from motivated parity-sensitive structural constraints.
